newsitem.title: CROATIA: Short kuna supply pushes up Croatian money rates.
newsitem.headline: Short kuna supply pushes up Croatian money rates.

text.p: Shortage of kuna funds continued to plague Croatia's money trade on Monday, further pushing up the interbank rates, dealers said.
"Again, demand is extremely strong and supply has already been exhausted," one dealer told Reuters.
Most of 28.8 million kuna demand was for term loans, struck at 14 and 15 percent, with call money making up 10 million kuna of the morning trade.
Call money went up another percentage point to 11 percent, after Friday's rise to 10 from 9.0 percent.
Overnight trade at the weekend totalled 55.2 million kuna and most were used for maintaining statutory reserves.
There were no interventions by the central bank. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557
